es: Separar hechos verificables, opiniones e insinuaciones en noticias y publicaciones, fijándose en las palabras que empujan al lector.

teaching.en: According to the survey, sixty per cent of residents use the library every week.
teaching.es: Según la encuesta, el sesenta por ciento de los residentes usa la biblioteca cada semana.
teaching.explanationEs: Según una fuente + una cifra: se trata de un dato que se puede comprobar.
segments: According to the survey, sixty per cent
of residents use the library every week.
teaching.audioText: According to the survey, sixty per cent of residents use the library every week.

teaching.en: The new timetable is obviously a terrible idea.
teaching.es: El nuevo horario es obviamente una idea terrible.
teaching.explanationEs: Obviously y terrible no describen un dato: expresan un juicio personal.
teaching.audioText: The new timetable is obviously a terrible idea.

teaching.en: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact: you can verify it in the council records.
teaching.es: La cifra de doscientas quejas es un hecho: puedes comprobarla en los registros del ayuntamiento.
teaching.explanationEs: Un fact se puede verificar con registros, fechas o cifras.
segments: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact:
you can verify it in the council records.
teaching.audioText: The figure of two hundred complaints is a fact: you can verify it in the council records.

teaching.en: The report does not say the mayor lied, but the headline seems to imply it.
teaching.es: El informe no dice que el alcalde mintió, pero el titular parece darlo a entender.
teaching.explanationEs: Imply = sugerir sin afirmar; seems to imply marca una insinuación.
segments: The report does not say the mayor lied,
but the headline seems to imply it.
teaching.audioText: The report does not say the mayor lied, but the headline seems to imply it.

teaching.en: Without evidence, a claim is only an opinion.
teaching.es: Sin pruebas, una afirmación es solo una opinión.
teaching.explanationEs: Evidence son las pruebas; sin ellas, lo que alguien afirma queda como opinión.
teaching.audioText: Without evidence, a claim is only an opinion.

prompt.es: ¿Cuál de estos enunciados es un hecho verificable?

choices.text: The library opens at nine on weekdays.
The library is the best place in town.
The library should stay open all night.

feedback.es: Un horario se puede comprobar; las otras dos frases expresan un juicio o un deseo personal.

hint.es: Un hecho se puede comprobar con un horario, una cifra o un registro.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una afirmación sin pruebas no se puede comprobar.»

feedback.es: Evidence son las pruebas que permiten verificar una afirmación.

hint.es: Es lo que necesitas para poder comprobar lo que alguien afirma.

origin.text: A claim without ___ cannot be checked.

prompt.es: Ordena: «El titular parece insinuar que el alcalde mintió.»

answer.text: The headline seems to imply the mayor lied

feedback.es: Seems to imply marca una insinuación: sugiere algo sin afirmarlo.

hint.es: La insinuación se construye con seems to + el verbo imply.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase del texto es una opinión y no un hecho?

choices.text: Seven want a new park.
The park is obviously a waste of money.
Ten neighbours answered the survey.

feedback.es: La frase del gasto usa obviously y un juicio; las otras dos son datos de la encuesta.

origin.text: Ten neighbours answered the survey. Seven want a new park. The park is obviously a waste of money, wrote one of them.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada enunciado con su tipo.

pairs: Forty students joined the trip, according to the school records.
The trip was obviously a waste of time.
The teacher, a friend of the bus company, chose the cheapest bus.

feedback.es: Los registros escolares dan un dato comprobable, obviously marca un juicio y la amistad con la empresa sugiere un favor.

pairs: Forty students joined the trip, according to the school records.
The trip was obviously a waste of time.
The teacher, a friend of the bus company, chose the cheapest bus.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué parte de la publicación se puede verificar.

choices.text: The idea that the mayor wastes money.
The idea that the pool is too big.
The amount the pool cost.

feedback.es: El coste de la piscina es una cifra que se puede comprobar; lo de malgastar dinero es un juicio con obviously.

origin.audio: Mia read a post about the new swimming pool. It said the pool had cost two hundred thousand dollars. The post also said the mayor was obviously wasting money.

prompt.es: ¿Qué enunciado de la reseña se puede verificar?

choices.text: The new cinema opened on 3 May.
The film was boring.
The seats are terrible.

feedback.es: Una fecha de apertura se comprueba; «boring» y «terrible» son juicios personales.

origin.text: The new cinema opened on 3 May. Honestly, the film was boring, and the seats are terrible.

prompt.es: ¿Qué insinúa el titular aunque no lo afirme?

choices.text: That the mayor drove the bus.
That the contract was a favour to a relative.
That the company was the cheapest.

feedback.es: Mencionar al primo del alcalde sugiere un favor; que fuera la empresa más barata es un hecho del artículo, no una insinuación.

origin.text: Headline: Mayor's cousin wins bus contract. Article: The council chose the cheapest company.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige por qué Mia no acepta lo que dice Leo.

choices.text: Because she thinks Leo is lying about the rubbish.
Because she has never seen the lake.
Because a little rubbish does not prove the lake is dirty.

feedback.es: Mia pide pruebas y dice que un poco de basura no basta para verificar la afirmación.

origin.audio: Leo says the lake is dirty. Mia answers: show me some proof. Leo says he saw some rubbish there last week. Mia says some rubbish is not enough to prove the claim.

prompt.es: Completa tres frases sobre cómo distinguir hechos y opiniones.

feedback.es: Un hecho se puede probar, las palabras de juicio delatan una opinión y para verificar una afirmación se buscan registros, fechas o cifras.

sentences: A ___ is something you can prove with a date or a figure.
Words like obviously often show an ___.
To ___ a claim, look for records, dates or numbers.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Según la encuesta, la mitad de los vecinos usa el parque.»

answer.text: According to the survey half of the neighbours use the park

feedback.es: Según una fuente se dice according to + fuente; después va el dato: half of the neighbours.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase es una opinión y no un hecho?

choices.text: The museum is obviously too expensive.
The museum charges eight dollars.
The museum closes at five.

feedback.es: Obviously y too expensive expresan un juicio; el precio y la hora de cierre se pueden comprobar.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué frase es una opinión.

choices.text: That the school has two hundred students.
That the canteen's pizza is better than any other.
That the article is two pages long.

feedback.es: «The best pizza in town» es un juicio personal; el número de alumnos es un dato.

origin.audio: The article says the school has two hundred students, and that the canteen serves the best pizza in town.
